HISTORY MEETS INNOVATION AT THE BROOKLYN NAVY YARD’S ANNUAL OPEN HOUSE! (SPONSORED)
Brooklyn Navy Yard’s Annual Open House
Saturday, October 17
12-5pm
FREE
Check in at Building 77, 141 Flushing Ave
Discover the Brooklyn Navy Yard’s 300-acre innovative campus during their
Annual Open House
, part of Open House New York Weekend on October 17 from 12-5pm. Step inside the studios of businesses in fashion, design, and technology for exclusive behind-the-scenes access, along with wine tastings, food trucks, live art demos, and more.
This year, two unique tour tracks have been created to guide visitors on their journeys:
Creative Currents
– Creativity flows through the Brooklyn Navy Yard; home to hundreds of artists, ranging from painters to photographers to jewelers. They’ll be opening their studios to the public, inviting audiences in for a rare opportunity to view their work, learn about their processes, inspirations, and their journeys here at the Yard.
BNY Past, Present, and Future
– From our start in 1801 as a premiere ship building facility, the Navy Yard has always been on the cutting edge of manufacturing and technology. On BNY’s campus, rich history meets an innovative future, as we look ahead towards what’s next in the fields of space tech, green energy, robotics, and more. Come tour BNY’s waterfront campus and take in centuries of legacy, as well as the labs and studios where the tech of the future is being made.
No matter what route you choose, this day celebrates a dynamic campus of makers and offers artists, engineers, entrepreneurs, and neighbors alike the chance to connect, meet the businesses who call the Navy Yard home, and experience innovation up close.

Title: TUES-THURS, 9/22-24: CJ HENDRY’S FLOWER MARKET, 27TH ON SALE, UNIVERSITY OPEN AIR, LOTS OF ART, AND MORE

TUES-THURS, 9/22-24: CJ HENDRY’S FLOWER MARKET, 27TH ON SALE, UNIVERSITY OPEN AIR, LOTS OF ART, AND MORE
tuesday
sponsored
: thru 10/3:
fall for dance festival at new york city center
: featuring 11 premieres and seven international companies, this year’s festival brings the world’s best from across the globe to city center—all for just $30. this is your chance to see international greats like the royal ballet and gauthier dance, or hometown heroes like robbie fairchild and a.i.m by kyle abraham. plus, a world premiere from off-broadway sensation pony cam (
burnout paradise
). see the world’s best, at a price you can’t beat. fall in love with dance and secure your seats today!
>>
sponsored
: thru 9/27:
myrtle avenue negroni week: a classic cocktail with local flavor
: bitter, bold + anything but ordinary! negroni week returns to myrtle avenue, with 10 bars and restaurants across fort greene and clinton hill putting their own spin on the iconic cocktail. this year, bartenders venture beyond the classic trio of gin, campari and sweet vermouth with mezcal, cherry, coffee, chocolate, rhubarb, mushrooms, orgeat…and even tomato, basil and olive oil. drink for a cause! each participating venue has also made a donation to slow food as part of negroni week’s global fundraising initiative.
cheers, salute, salud and sláinte
…negroni week is back on myrtle avenue!
>>
tues 6pm (monthly thru 12/1):
miller theater’s pop-up concert series
: sit onstage with virtuoso musicians during columbia university school of the arts’s hour-long early-evening concerts, with a free drink in hand and the opportunity to mingle with the performers afterward. the 15th season kicks off tonight with a celebration of hungarian composer györgy kurtág’s 100th birthday, featuring soprano tony arnold, violinist christopher otto, and pianist amy williams. miller theatre at columbia university (morningside heights), free admission.
>>
tues 6-10pm:
summerstage: music for action, a climate week concert
: the city parks foundation wraps up its free summerstage programming with a climate week concert featuring performances by young the giant, st. lucia, and dreeemy (dj set). presented in partnership with lymelnk and supported by the steven + alexandra cohen foundation’s cohen lyme + tickborne disease initiative, the concert raises awareness about climate change and the resulting increase in tick-borne diseases, including in urban areas and city parks.
>>
tues 7pm (monthly):
brooklyn books + booze
: hear established and up-and-coming authors of different genres read from their current works every third tuesday of the month at barrow’s intense tasting room (industry city). tonight’s lineup includes megan frampton, carol gyzander, micaiah johnson, and mia v. moss. free admission.
>>
tues 7pm (monthly):
we love a theme: a storytelling show
: a lineup of performers tell funny, heartwarming, and cringe-inducing tales at bailey swilley’s monthly storytelling show. tonight’s ‘lesson learned’ theme features mitch applebaum, eleanora ko, henry suarez, and julia whitehouse. pete’s candy store (williamsburg), free ($5 suggested donation).
>>
tues 7pm:
i’ll have the bisque! a benefit comedy show for abortion access
: join improv troupe the bisque and guests for a comedy show raising money for abortion access. special guests include comedians dylan adler (comedy central), jaydan heather (‘jaydan heather’s cuntry’), and improv group go dummy!, and ticket proceeds will support the brigid alliance, a nonprofit that provides logistical support to people who must travel long distances for abortion care. caveat (les), $13.61 with promo code ‘skint’ (reg. $18.76-20).
>>
tues 9:30pm:
impossible new york stories
: every new yorker has had a crazy moment that makes them say, ‘only in new york…’ hear comedians and storytellers share their wildest, strangest, and yet totally true – impossible new york stories. hosted by laura canty-samuel. $13.61 with promo code ‘skint’ (reg. $24-25).
>>

THE NONSENSE LAB
from September 17 to October 3 in the Doxsee Theater. For three weeks, join us for a Festival of new work, exploring how we can create poetry and beauty through nonsense itself.  Lead Artists examine the nonsensical world around us while grappling with themes of humanity, isolation, and memories through music, dance, performance, puppetry, and toy theater. The Laboratory is anchored by three productions lead by
Caroline Fermin, Adam M. Kassim, and Kathleen Kennedy Tobin
, each for 6 performances, and three 1-time events by
Theresa Buchheister, Saskia Lane
, and a
TMT Community Café
.
The Nonsense Lab
runs September 17 through October 3 at the Doxsee Theater in Sunset Park, Brooklyn.

anora
,
kpop demon hunters
,
disability + visibility

the stringer: the man who took the photo

cutting through rocks

27th on sale

clueless
costume designer mona may at book signings on wednesday, get free embroidery and monogramming on thursday, and more. proceeds benefit fit student scholarships and creative programs. fit’s john e. reeves great hall (chelsea), free-$25 admission.

brooklyn contra

the new york times
, 2026 pulitzer prize winner for opinion writing), steven feldstein (the carnegie endowment for international peace), and sarah myers west (ai now institute), with moderator ilia venyavkin (kronika). craig newmark graduate school of journalism at cuny (midtown), free admission.

:

lack history

sesame street

art + furniture: designers, makers, and advocates

i am tony
, the artist’s most comprehensive survey to date,

, tracing the history of art and visual culture along the bowery, diego marcon’s
arrivederci, piggies!

260 madison art exhibition

university open air: fall edition

cj hendry’s flower market

untitled (art car)

ric burns and james sanders — ‘new york: the future of cities’ — rebuilding lower manhattan

new york: a documentary film

wonder wheel

the dead ladies show nyc
: the bimonthly dead ladies show features presentations on three deceased dames who made an impact on the world during their lifetimes. tonight’s subjects: indira gandhi, mary shelly, and maria callas. the private curtain at kgb (les), $10 adv, $15 door.

colbert

loud about nothing podcast

bring the funny

golden spiral comedy show
: at mindy raf and katie compa’s golden spiral comedy show, stand-up set lengths follow the fibonacci sequence (5, 8, 13, and 21 minutes each). tonight’s show at whiskey cellar nyc (east village) features max cohen (siriusxm), darin patterson (
snl nerds
), mike drucker (
samantha bee
), calvin cato (netflix), and leah bonnema (
colbert

niche night: y2k baby one more time
: throwback to the 90s and early 00s with djs cor and steve reynolds of party like it’s 1999 spinning pop, r+b, rock, and dance floor favorites. request open. friends and lovers (crown heights), free admission.

awkward teenage years
: laugh and reminisce as storytellers relive their growing-up joys and traumas for your entertainment. hosted by grant bowen and featuring stories by carly ann filbin, azhar bande-ali, ann chun, and eleanor ko. under st. marks (east village), pay-what-you-can admission ($7 min).

crystal visions – stevie nicks’ greatest hits
: prideshow at the sideshow and sissy fist present a magical evening of drag artists honoring stevie nicks, featuring performances of her hits ‘silver springs,’ ‘stop draggin’ my heart around,’ ‘landslide,’ ‘edge of seventeen,’ and more. sideshows by the seashore (coney island), $20.

landline comedy at wild east brewing co.

(gowanus). tonight’s lineup includes daniela mora, rojo perez, bridget mcguir, orion levine, and molly ruben-long. hosted by andre medrano. bonus: rsvp for a chance to win a free drink. free admission.

Content:
MYRTLE AVENUE NEGRONI WEEK 2026 (SPONSORED)
Myrtle Avenue Negroni Week 2026
September 21–27
Bitter, Bold & Anything But Ordinary!
Negroni Week returns to Myrtle Avenue September 21–27, with
10 bars and restaurants across Fort Greene and Clinton Hill
putting their own spin on the iconic cocktail. This year, bartenders venture beyond the classic trio of gin, Campari and sweet vermouth with mezcal, cherry, coffee, chocolate, rhubarb, mushrooms, orgeat…and even tomato, basil and olive oil.
Here’s what’s mixing
:
•
Doppelgänger
–
The Triangle In The Square
: A smoky, ruby-red mezcal riff with Cocchi Americano, Averna and rhubarb bitters.
•
The Emerson
–
City-Sangue Cherry Negroni
: A deep-red, cherry-forward blend of Citadelle Jardin d’Été, Campari, sweet vermouth and Luxardo Sangue Morlacco.
•
LaRina Pastificio & Vino
–
Diavolo in Me
: Bright, bittersweet and slightly sour, with gin, Italian bitters, lemon, orgeat—and a little devil in it.
•
Little Falcon
–
House Negroni
: The Italian classic heads in a distinctly French direction, with a touch of French elegance.
•
Lula Mae Sporting Club
–
Three Ways to Negroni
: Choose from Classic, bright and botanical White, or smoky Mezcal.
•
Neno’s
–
El Ahumadito Negroni
: Poblano-infused mezcal gives this one a smoky Mexican spin. Try the
$22 El Ahumadito Experience
, pairing it with a pork belly taco.
•
Osteria Brooklyn
–
Smoked Negroni
: Gray Whale Gin, made with California-sourced botanicals, gives this riff its West Coast character.
•
Putnam’s Pub
–
Wild Rose Negroni
: Featuring Glendalough Wild Rose Gin, made with rose petals from the garden of owner Gerry Rooney’s late mother, Rose.
•
Rosticceria Evelina
–
Five Ways to Negroni
: Five inventive riffs include coffee, chocolate and the savory Negroni Pie with olive oil-washed gin, tomato-infused Campari and basil vermouth.
•
Vine
–
Shroom Negroni
: An earthy, umami-rich riff combining gin, Campari and Carpano Antica with Veda mushroom liqueur and shiitake mushroom syrup, finished with ground shiitake and an edible flower.
Drink for a cause! Each participating venue has also made a donation to
Slow Food
as part of Negroni Week’s global fundraising initiative.
Ten locations. Seven days. Countless ways to Negroni.
Cheers, salute, salud and sláinte
…Negroni Week is back on Myrtle Avenue!

Title: RIC BURNS AND JAMES SANDERS — “NEW YORK: THE FUTURE OF CITIES”  — REBUILDING LOWER MANHATTAN

Content:
RIC BURNS AND JAMES SANDERS — “NEW YORK: THE FUTURE OF CITIES”  — REBUILDING LOWER MANHATTAN
What does the future of a city look like — and how does its past shape what’s possible?
On Thursday, September 24 at 6 p.m., join the Downtown Alliance and Pace University for a screening of highlights from Ric Burns and James Sanders’ new two-part documentary series:
“New York: The Future of Cities.”
With these episodes, Burns and Sanders continue their original award-winning eight-part, 17-1/2-hour series, “New York: A Documentary Film,” which originally aired on PBS between 1999 and 2003.
TICKETS HERE
The screening will be followed by a conversation with Burns, Sanders and Vishaan Chakrabarti, architect and founder of PAU (Practice for Architecture and Urbanism).
Spanning the first two decades of the 21st century, “The Future of Cities” captures a New York in the midst of remarkable transformation, from the aftermath of September 11 to the city’s emergence as a global “superstar city.” Along the way, the film explores the challenges that cities everywhere now face, including infrastructure, immigration, governance, equity, financial crises, climate change and resilience.
At the heart of this story is Lower Manhattan, a neighborhood whose transformation over the past 25 years has helped shape the trajectory of the city itself. From the rebuilding of the World Trade Center site and the creation of new public spaces to the growth of a vibrant residential, cultural and commercial district, Lower Manhattan has undergone one of the most significant urban transformations in modern New York.
This special evening will take a closer look at how and why Lower Manhattan was rebuilt, the choices and ideas that shaped its transformation and its place in the broader story of New York’s evolution. Through the lens of “The Future of Cities,” the discussion will explore what the rebuilding of Lower Manhattan reveals about New York’s resilience, creativity and capacity to continually reinvent itself.
Ric Burns
, a scholar trustee of the New York Historical, is the founder of Steeplechase Films and an internationally recognized documentary filmmaker co-writer and producer of “The Civil War” and “New York: A Documentary Film.”
Vishaan Chakrabarti
is an architect and founder and creative director of PAU (Practice for Architecture and Urbanism), where he leads the firm’s portfolio of cultural, institutional and public projects, which include the redesign of New York’s Penn Station, designer of the Domino Sugar Refinery and designing the FAA’s sustainable air traffic control tower prototype. Chakrabarti has over 30 years of urban architecture experience, including president of Moynihan Station Venture at The Related Companies and director of the New York Department of City Planning’s Manhattan office. He has also been dean of University of California, Berkeley’s College of Environmental Design and a professor at Columbia University’s architecture school. Chakrabarti is the author of “A Country of Cities: A Manifesto for an Urban America” and “The Architecture of Urbanity: Designing for Nature, Culture, and Joy.” In 2025, he was awarded the Edmund N. Bacon Urban Design Award.
James Sanders, FAIA
, is the architect behind the design and research firm James Sanders Studio, as well as an author and filmmaker. With Ric Burns, he wrote and produced “New York: A Documentary Film,” and its companion book, “New York: An Illustrated History.”

THE KLEZMATICS & FRIENDS 40TH ANNIVERSARY CONCERT (SPONSORED)
For four decades, these GRAMMY-winning trailblazers have redefined Yiddish music for new generations, blending deep tradition with fearless creativity and a spirit of joy, resilience, and social change. Join us for a one-night-only celebration featuring special guests, longtime collaborators, and music spanning their remarkable 40-year journey of radical joy with a legacy unlike any other in contemporary roots music.
The evening will feature music from all of The Klezmatics’ fourteen recordings, including their GRAMMY Award-winning album,
Wonder Wheel
with lyrics by Woody Guthrie, with a special focus on Woody Guthrie’s inspiring texts, and The Klezmatics’ collaborations with Guthrie.
Special guests include Janis Ian, Lavender Light Gospel Choir, Susan McKeown, Danny Blume, and more!
